news.headline_zh: 肠道病毒 D68 暴发引发哮喘儿童健康担忧。
news.lead_zh: 近期美国多地废水样本中检测到 EV-D68 浓度升高,尤其在中西部、东北和南部地区,引发对哮喘儿童健康风险的关注。
key_findings_zh: EV-D68 在美国废水样本中浓度达到自追踪开始以来的最高水平。
EV-D68 主要影响儿童,尤其是哮喘患者,可能引发严重呼吸问题。
WastewaterSCAN 指出 EV-D68 在社区中广泛传播,但未统计实际患病人数。
EV-D68 与罕见的急性弛缓性脊髓炎 (AFM) 有关,但病例仍较少。
公共卫生建议加强手部卫生以减少病毒传播风险。
news.trend_or_risk_zh: EV-D68 在美国出现反季节传播趋势,对儿童健康构成潜在风险。
news.caveats_zh: 废水监测数据仅反映社区传播趋势,无法预测个体感染情况。
news.headline_en: EV-D68 Outbreak Raises Concerns for Asthmatic Children.
news.lead_en: Recent wastewater samples in the U.S. show EV-D68 reaching some of the highest levels since tracking began, raising concerns for children with asthma.
key_findings_en: EV-D68 reached some of the highest wastewater levels since tracking began in September 2023.
The virus is particularly concerning for children with asthma, as it can trigger severe breathing problems.
WastewaterSCAN classified EV-D68 as high nationally, indicating widespread community spread.
Acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare complication, remains uncommon despite the virus's prevalence.
Public health experts recommend families of asthmatic children to prepare for potential outbreaks.
news.trend_or_risk_en: EV-D68 is showing an out-of-season resurgence in the U.S., posing a risk to children, especially those with asthma.
news.caveats_en: Wastewater data provides a signal of community spread but does not reflect individual cases or predict outbreak severity.
news.brief_en: The article from Medical Daily, published on October 8, 2026, reports that EV-D68 reached some of the highest wastewater levels since tracking began in September 2023. In September 2026, EV-D68 was detected in about 72% of U.S. wastewater samples, up from 20% in August 2026. WastewaterSCAN classified the virus as high nationally, indicating its spread in communities. However, the data does not count sick individuals or predict the number of children needing care. The main concern is for children with asthma, as EV-D68 can trigger severe breathing problems. A rare complication, acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), which causes sudden limb weakness, remains uncommon. The article emphasizes the need for families of children with asthma to prepare, but no specific actions or outcomes are confirmed. The situation is under investigation, and the data is based on wastewater monitoring, which provides a signal of community spread but not individual cases.

papers.title: A versatile and stable reporter platform for human rhinovirus and other enteroviruses
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human rhinovirus (HRV), a major cause of upper respiratory infections, has increasingly been associated with lower respiratory tract disease. Although tools to investigate HRV pathogenesis are needed, they remain limited. Reporter viruses expressing fluorescent or luminescent proteins are powerful tools for analyzing viral distribution and replication; however, insertion of a reporter gene often impairs viral replication, and the inserted gene is readily lost during serial passage. To address these problems, we established a versatile and stable strategy for generating reporter HRV and other enteroviruses. The gene encoding mScarlet3, a red fluorescent protein, was inserted between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene, a site previously used in other enteroviruses but not in HRV. Optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence between mScarlet3 and VP4 yielded a reporter HRV with growth kinetics comparable to those of the wild-type virus. To improve the genetic stability of the reporter insert, we evaluated GC-content optimization of the reporter gene and relocation of the cis-acting replication element (CRE). GC-content optimization substantially improved reporter stability in both HRV-B14 and EV-A71, whereas CRE relocation provided additional stabilization in EV-A71 but not in HRV-B14, demonstrating the potential applicability of this strategy to other enteroviruses. This strategy for constructing stable reporter HRV and other enteroviruses will facilitate studies of enterovirus pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Human rhinovirus (HRV) has lacked a reporter system expressing widely used reporter proteins, such as GFP, that enables visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues. The only reporter HRV reported to date loses fluorescence upon fixation and tolerates only small inserts, limiting its utility. Meanwhile, the clinical importance of HRV has become increasingly recognized, as reflected by its high detection rate among hospitalized children and recent outbreaks associated with fatal cases. A versatile and stable strategy for constructing reporter HRV is therefore urgently needed. Here, we overcome the two major obstacles to generating stable reporter HRV - impaired viral replication and loss of the inserted gene - and demonstrate that this strategy is also applicable to other enteroviruses. By providing a broadly applicable framework for constructing stable reporter viruses, this work establishes a foundation for visualizing infection dynamics and studying the pathogenesis of HRV and other enteroviruses.

Reporter viruses expressing fluorescent or luminescent proteins are powerful tools for analyzing viral distribution and replication; however, insertion of a reporter gene often impairs viral replication, and the inserted gene is readily lost during serial passage. To address these problems, we established a versatile and stable strategy for generating reporter HRV and other enteroviruses. The gene encoding mScarlet3, a red fluorescent protein, was inserted between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene, a site previously used in other enteroviruses but not in HRV. Optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence between mScarlet3 and VP4 yielded a reporter HRV with growth kinetics comparable to those of the wild-type virus. To improve the genetic stability of the reporter insert, we evaluated GC-content optimization of the reporter gene and relocation of the cis-acting replication element (CRE). GC-content optimization substantially improved reporter stability in both HRV-B14 and EV-A71, whereas CRE relocation provided additional stabilization in EV-A71 but not in HRV-B14, demonstrating the potential applicability of this strategy to other enteroviruses. This strategy for constructing stable reporter HRV and other enteroviruses will facilitate studies of enterovirus pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Human rhinovirus (HRV) has lacked a reporter system expressing widely used reporter proteins, such as GFP, that enables visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues. The only reporter HRV reported to date loses fluorescence upon fixation and tolerates only small inserts, limiting its utility. Meanwhile, the clinical importance of HRV has become increasingly recognized, as reflected by its high detection rate among hospitalized children and recent outbreaks associated with fatal cases. A versatile and stable strategy for constructing reporter HRV is therefore urgently needed. Here, we overcome the two major obstacles to generating stable reporter HRV - impaired viral replication and loss of the inserted gene - and demonstrate that this strategy is also applicable to other enteroviruses. By providing a broadly applicable framework for constructing stable reporter viruses, this work establishes a foundation for visualizing infection dynamics and studying the pathogenesis of HRV and other enteroviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human rhinovirus (HRV) has increasingly been associated with lower respiratory tract disease, yet tools to investigate HRV pathogenesis remain limited. The lack of a robust reporter system for HRV has hindered the visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study aimed to address the limitations of existing reporter systems by developing a versatile and stable strategy for generating reporter HRV and other enteroviruses. This strategy was evaluated for its applicability to HRV-B14 and EV-A71, which are representative of non-polio human enteroviruses.
analysis.methods: To improve the genetic stability of the reporter insert, the researchers evaluated GC-content optimization of the reporter gene and relocation of the cis-acting replication element (CRE). They inserted the mScarlet3 gene between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene, optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence to ensure viral replication was not impaired.
analysis.main_results: GC-content optimization substantially improved reporter stability in both HRV-B14 and EV-A71. CRE relocation provided additional stabilization in EV-A71 but not in HRV-B14, demonstrating the potential applicability of this strategy to other enteroviruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as demonstrating a successful strategy to overcome the two major obstacles to generating stable reporter HRV - impaired viral replication and loss of the inserted gene. This approach provides a broadly applicable framework for constructing stable reporter viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This strategy for constructing stable reporter HRV and other enteroviruses will facilitate studies of enterovirus pathogenesis, offering new insights into viral dynamics and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not report limitations, but the evidence is based on direct observations of reporter stability and growth kinetics, which are comparable to those of the wild-type virus. The findings are supported by target-specific methods and results.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a versatile and stable reporter platform for human rhinovirus (HRV) and other enteroviruses, addressing the limitations of existing reporter systems. The researchers inserted a red fluorescent protein gene (mScarlet3) between the 5′UTR and VP4 gene of HRV-B14 and EV-A71, optimizing the 2A cleavage sequence to maintain viral replication. GC-content optimization improved reporter stability in both viruses, while CRE relocation enhanced stability in EV-A71 but not HRV-B14. The strategy enables visualization of viral dynamics in infected cells and tissues, offering new tools for studying enterovirus pathogenesis. The findings are based on direct observations of reporter stability and growth kinetics, demonstrating the potential applicability of this method to other enteroviruses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人鼻病毒 (HRV) 与下呼吸道疾病的关联性日益增强,但研究 HRV 发病机制 的工具仍然有限。由于缺乏强大的 HRV 报告系统,阻碍了受感染细胞和组织中病毒动态的可视化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究旨在通过开发一种通用且稳定的策略来生成报告 HRV 和其他肠道病毒,从而解决现有报告系统的局限性。该策略针对 HRV-B14 和 EV-A71(代表非脊髓灰质炎 人肠道病毒)的适用性进行了评估。
elements_zh.methods: 为了提高报告基因插入片段的遗传稳定性,研究人员评估了报告基因的GC含量优化和顺式作用复制元件(CRE)的重新定位。他们将 mScarlet3 基因插入到 5'UTR 和 VP4 基因之间,优化 2A 切割序列以确保病毒复制不受影响。
elements_zh.main_results: GC 含量优化显着提高了 HRV-B14 和 EV-A71 中报告基因的稳定性。CRE 重定位在 EV-A71 中提供了额外的稳定性,但在 HRV-B14 中没有,这表明该策略对其他肠道病毒的潜在适用性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为证明了一种成功的策略,可以克服产生稳定报告 HRV 的两个主要障碍——病毒复制受损和插入基因丢失。这种方法为构建稳定的报告病毒提供了广泛适用的框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这种构建稳定的报告 HRV 和其他肠道病毒的策略将促进肠道病毒 发病机制 的研究,为病毒动力学和潜在治疗靶点提供新的见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究没有报告局限性,但证据是基于对报告者稳定性和生长动力学的直接观察,这些结果与野生型病毒相当。这些发现得到了针对具体目标的方法和结果的支持。

papers.title: Complement-related gene polymorphisms and severity of Coxsackievirus A6-induced hand, foot, and mouth disease in chinese han children: a candidate-gene association study
papers.abstract: Severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) remains an important threat to child health. Host genetic factors, particularly those involved in complement activation, may contribute to HFMD susceptibility, but the role of complement-related gene polymorphisms in disease severity remains unclear. We enrolled 189 children with Coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6)-induced HFMD from Henan Children’s Hospital, including 94 severe and 95 mild cases. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes using a modified phenol-chloroform method, and SNP genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP. Crude and multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age group and sex were used to evaluate associations between SNP genotypes and severe HFMD. In models adjusted for age group and sex, nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD were observed for C5 rs3761847 GA versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.523, 95% CI: 1.036–6.143), C3 rs2250656 TC versus TT (adjusted OR = 1.982, 95% CI: 1.061–3.704), and CFH rs1065489 TT versus GG (adjusted OR = 3.125, 95% CI: 1.249–7.818) and GT versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.499, 95% CI: 1.118–5.588). However, none of these associations remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. The combined SNP model showed limited discriminatory performance, with an apparent AUC of 0.653 and a bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC of 0.631. Exploratory genotype-related differences were also observed in selected laboratory parameters. C5, C3, and CFH variants showed nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD in this exploratory candidate-gene study, but these findings did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Further validation in larger independent cohorts is required.

papers.title_zh: 中国汉族儿童柯萨奇病毒A6所致手足口病补体相关基因多态性与严重程度的候选基因关联研究
papers.source_body_en: Severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) remains an important threat to child health. Host genetic factors, particularly those involved in complement activation, may contribute to HFMD susceptibility, but the role of complement-related gene polymorphisms in disease severity remains unclear. We enrolled 189 children with Coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6)-induced HFMD from Henan Children’s Hospital, including 94 severe and 95 mild cases. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes using a modified phenol-chloroform method, and SNP genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP. Crude and multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age group and sex were used to evaluate associations between SNP genotypes and severe HFMD. In models adjusted for age group and sex, nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD were observed for C5 rs3761847 GA versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.523, 95% CI: 1.036–6.143), C3 rs2250656 TC versus TT (adjusted OR = 1.982, 95% CI: 1.061–3.704), and CFH rs1065489 TT versus GG (adjusted OR = 3.125, 95% CI: 1.249–7.818) and GT versus GG (adjusted OR = 2.499, 95% CI: 1.118–5.588). However, none of these associations remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. The combined SNP model showed limited discriminatory performance, with an apparent AUC of 0.653 and a bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC of 0.631. Exploratory genotype-related differences were also observed in selected laboratory parameters. C5, C3, and CFH variants showed nominal associations with severe CVA6-induced HFMD in this exploratory candidate-gene study, but these findings did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Further validation in larger independent cohorts is required.

papers.full_text: Nature Reviews Microbiology nature reviews microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 Review article Check for updates Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses Hendrik Jan Thibaut 1, Dirk Jochmans 1,3, Christophe Van Dijck2,3, Manon Laporte 1,3, Laurens Liesenborghs 2 & Johan Neyts1 Abstract Small molecule antiviral drugs have transformed the management of infections such as those caused by HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, herpesviruses and influenza viruses. Effective antiviral therapeutics remain unavailable for many other often life-threatening viral infections, many of which are caused by RNA viruses. The development of potent, safe and orally available antivirals is therefore essential both to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for building a diversified portfolio of broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families or even crossing viral families. We provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses and discuss the biological determinants that underlie their antiviral spectrum. Finally, we outline the clinical development frameworks required to accelerate the evaluation of such drugs, in particular in the context of outbreaks. Sections Introduction One drug to treat them all? Direct-acting antivirals versus host-targeting antivirals New approaches to discover new targets for broader-acting antivirals Translational readiness Conclusions 1KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Leuven, Belgium. 2Department of Clinical Sciences, Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, Belgium. 3These authors contributed equally: Dirk Jochmans, Christophe Van Dijck, Manon Laporte. e-mail: johan.neyts@kuleuven.be Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article Alongside vaccine development, sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery is therefore essential. Antiviral drug development has so far largely been focused on viral infections that offer large and predict- able commercial markets (for example, those caused by HIV and HCV). It is obviously unrealistic and economically unsustainable to develop specific antiviral drugs for each known viral pathogen. Newly emerging viruses will most likely belong to viral families already known (Table 1) today. Advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing greatly expanded our understanding of viral diversity, and although new viral families may still be discovered, such events are becoming increasingly rare. Together, this strongly supports a strategy in which broader-acting small molecule antiviral (BSA) drugs are developed. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. Therefore, it cannot be guaranteed that efficacious vaccines can always be developed when new threatening viruses emerge4,5. mAbs can offer immediate protection and are transforming the prophylaxis or treatment of certain acute viral diseases, such as those caused by the rabies virus6 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)7. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. Box 1 | Categories and examples of broader-spectrum antivirals (BSAs) for RNA viruses Cross-family BSAs Active against viruses belonging to different (related or unrelated) viral families or across a certain genome architecture (that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA viruses)), typically by targeting conserved features of the viral replication machinery such as the catalytic site of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases. For example, remdesivir, a nucleoside viral polymerase inhibitor, is active against viruses belonging to different viral families, that is, the (−)ssRNA Filoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Pneumoviridae and Arenaviridae as well as the (+) ssRNA Flaviviridae, Picornaviridae and Coronaviridae. Baloxavir, an endonuclease inhibitor, inhibits influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae) but also, although much less potently, several members of the family Peribunyaviridae. Pan-family BSAs Active across all or at least most genera within a single viral family. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. Intra-family BSAs Can be active against multiple serotypes, genotypes or strains of a particular virus species. For example, mosnodenvir is active against all dengue virus genotypes (family Flaviviridae) by blocking the interaction between viral proteins NS4B and NS3. Intra-family broader-spectrum activity may span several viruses within one genus of a particular family without extending to other genera. For example, the non-covalent, non-peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor ensitrelvir is active only against members of the genus Betacoronavirus (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), SARS-CoV-1 and human coronavirus (HCoV)-OC43), but not against members of the genus Alphacoronavirus (such as HCoV-229E and HCoV-NL63) within the family Coronaviridae. Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article inhibitors) or active against one or more (but not all) genera of a viral family (Box 1). The need for broader-acting antivirals and their desired spectrum of activity are mostly defined by the particular (clinical) context (Boxes 2 and 3). For viruses that cause a high number of annual cases (for example, RSV), there might be a sufficiently large market, and thus incentives, to develop virus-specific drugs. Conversely, there might be no or less financial incentive to develop virus-specific drugs for viruses that cause a rather limited number of cases but that col- lectively, within their genus or family, are responsible for a substan- tial clinical burden (for example, coxsackieviruses and echoviruses, EV-D68 and EV-A71 that all belong to the genus Enterovirus). In this case, the development of antivirals that are broadly active across the entire Enterovirus genus (pan-Enterovirus; category intra-family BSAs) represents a more realistic approach. In the context of epidemic or pan- demic preparedness, access to pan-family and cross-family BSAs may be particularly important, as it cannot be predicted which viral family a newly emerging pathogen (‘virus X’) will belong to. Given the extensive genetic diversity and distinct replication strategies of viral families, the development of a single cross-family drug with potent activity against all RNA virus families is likely to be unrealistic. Rather, a more feasible strategy may be to establish a portfolio of different types of BSAs that collectively provide, either alone or in combination, coverage across the RNA virus landscape. BSAs may also be valuable in the context of viral co-infections, in which a single drug could simultaneously target two (or more) viruses14,15. Beyond the spectrum of activity, BSA development must be guided by clearly defined target product profiles16. To have a meaningful clinical impact, BSAs (or combinations thereof) should ideally be highly efficacious, be orally available (preferably once daily dosing), be safe for a broad patient population (preferably including pregnant women and children), possess a (relatively) high barrier to resistance and exhibit minimal drug–drug interactions16. Virus tissue tropism further influences desirable drug properties. For example, infections involving the central nervous system require efficient blood–brain barrier penetration, whereas limited penetration may be preferable for peripheral viral infections. Consequently, distinct target product profiles may be required, even within a single viral genus. TBEV, tick-borne encephalitis virus. Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article typically invade the central nerve system, whereas yellow fever virus and DENV do not17. The importance of preparedness against known viruses (such as EV-D6818, Ebola virus19, monkeypox virus20 and Andes hantavirus21) as well as against emerging viral threats (for example, SARS-CoV-2) has been repeatedly illustrated during outbreaks caused by these diverse viral pathogens. During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19 pan- demic), no antiviral drugs were available at the onset. A stockpile of an oral, pan-family coronavirus BSA before the start of the COVID-19 pan- demic would likely have saved countless lives22,23. Remdesivir, originally discovered as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) inhibitor of RSV24 and Ebola viruses25,26, was the only drug for which antiviral activity against coronaviruses had been systematically demonstrated in preclinical models before the pandemic27. In the absence of readily available and effective antiviral treat- ments, drug repurposing may need to be considered. Repurpos- ing can provide a rapid and relatively cost-effective response by leveraging de-risked drugs with existing preclinical and clinical safety data28,29. However, drugs developed or used for non-viral indi- cations are mostly unlikely to possess sufficient antiviral potency to curb outbreaks caused by newly emerging and (potentially highly) pathogenic viruses. At the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, extensive repurposing initiatives studied whether drugs approved for other indications could inhibit SARS-CoV-2 replication. Drugs such as azithro- mycin (antibiotic), itraconazole (antifungal), hydroxychloroquine (antimalarial, antirheumatic), niclosamide (anthelmintic), ivermectin (anthelmintic) and nitazoxanide (antiparasitic) rapidly entered numer- ous clinical trials, many of them small and underpowered, and even became, for some time, standard treatment in certain settings despite limited preclinical evidence30. Overall, drug repurposing efforts dur- ing the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic were largely unsuccessful, highlighting that such strategies should not be initiated only at the time a new virus emerges. A more realistic approach is to systematically assess existing drugs during epidemic or pandemic ‘peace-time’ against panels of viruses that are representative of high-risk families. Drugs with ‘reason- able’ in vitro activity can be further tested, alone or in combinations, in preclinical models13. Studies in SARS-CoV-2-infected hamsters revealed that combi- nations of two or three antivirals, each used at suboptimal or even inactive doses, can result in important antiviral effects31. To ration- ally develop combination strategies for BSAs, systematic preclinical testing of combinations across viral families is required. Extensive preclinical studies of the most promising combinations may help to guide strategies for stockpiling for epidemic or pandemic prepared- ness. The use of fixed-dose combinations (such as those used in the treatment of HIV infections) would be ideal. Yet, in outbreak situation with new pathogens, there will be insufficient time to develop such fixed-dose combinations; co-administration of individual drugs would therefore represent a more practical approach. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. Therefore, it cannot be guaranteed that efficacious vaccines can always be developed when new threatening viruses emerge4,5. mAbs can offer immediate protection and are transforming the prophylaxis or treatment of certain acute viral diseases, such as those caused by the rabies virus6 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)7. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. Box 1 | Categories and examples of broader-spectrum antivirals (BSAs) for RNA viruses Cross-family BSAs Active against viruses belonging to different (related or unrelated) viral families or across a certain genome architecture (that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA viruses)), typically by targeting conserved features of the viral replication machinery such as the catalytic site of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases. Baloxavir, an endonuclease inhibitor, inhibits influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae) but also, although much less potently, several members of the family Peribunyaviridae. Pan-family BSAs Active across all or at least most genera within a single viral family. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. papers.title_original: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, particularly human enteroviruses, with an emphasis on non-polio enteroviruses such as EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, CV-A16, and echoviruses. The central question is whether BSAs can be developed to target multiple RNA virus genera, families, or even cross families, and how this can address current unmet medical needs and improve pandemic preparedness.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods or meta-analysis. It provides a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses, including human enteroviruses, and discusses the biological determinants underlying their antiviral spectrum. The authors also outline the clinical development frameworks needed for evaluating such drugs, particularly in outbreak scenarios.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that developing BSAs is a viable strategy to address the limitations of current antiviral therapies for RNA viruses. It highlights the importance of targeting conserved viral components to achieve broad-spectrum activity and emphasizes the need for sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery to meet both current and future medical needs.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing have expanded our understanding of viral diversity, the development of BSAs remains challenging due to the complexity of viral biology and the need for precise targeting. There is a lack of comprehensive data on the efficacy and safety of BSAs in clinical settings, particularly for non-polio human enteroviruses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should prioritize the identification of conserved viral targets and the development of antiviral agents with broad-spectrum activity. It also recommends strengthening clinical development frameworks to enable rapid evaluation of BSAs during outbreaks, especially for viruses like EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, and CV-A16.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, with a focus on human enteroviruses such as EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, CV-A16, and echoviruses. It argues that creating BSAs is essential to address the lack of effective treatments for many RNA viruses and to improve pandemic preparedness. The review highlights the biological rationale for BSAs, discusses existing antiviral agents, and outlines the need for clinical frameworks to evaluate these drugs. However, it also identifies challenges, including the complexity of viral biology and the absence of robust clinical data. The implications emphasize the importance of targeting conserved viral components and accelerating research and development for BSAs, particularly in outbreak contexts.

papers.full_text: ABSTRACTEnterovirus 2B is a highly conserved, functionally versatile, nonstructural protein. The classic viroporin model, which restricts its role to ion channel formation, cannot account for its interactions with host factors such as Bcl-2-associated X protein, interleukin enhancer-binding factor 2, and karyopherin subunit alpha 1, nor its functional divergence among enteroviruses. We propose a novel, testable membrane stress sensor hypothesis: the transmembrane helices of 2B sense lipid composition and pH changes, and through conformational dynamics, spatiotemporally coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis, and immune evasion. We elaborate on this framework across six dimensions: structure–function mapping, calcium signaling, cell death pathways, immune evasion, evolutionary footprint, and antiviral targeting, along with cross-virus comparisons. We highlight key evidence gaps and limitations, and propose several future research directions. This framework establishes a mechanistic foundation for understanding 2B function and guiding rational anti-enteroviral drug designs. Supplementary MaterialSupplementary data.docx Conclusions and outlookThis study proposes an integrative framework in which the enterovirus 2B protein acts as a “membrane stress sensor,” thereby overcoming the limitations of the traditional viroporin model. Through conformational dynamics, the transmembrane helices of 2B sense changes in the membrane microenvironment (lipid composition, pH, and curvature) and coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, and immune evasion outputs in a spatiotemporally specific manner. Important human pathogens within this genus include coxsackieviruses, enterovirus A71 (EVA71), enterovirus D68 (EVD68), echoviruses, and poliovirus (PV) [7–9]. Although these viruses share characteristics such as a small genome, rapid evolution, and broad pathogenic spectrum, targeted antiviral drugs remain absent. The functional pleiotropy of nonstructural protein 2B has emerged as a major obstacle to rational drug design. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.Enteroviruses possess a single-stranded, positive-sense RNA genome of approximately 7.5 kb in length [10–12]. A single open reading frame encodes a polyprotein that is proteolytically processed into three precursor regions: P1 (structural proteins VP1–VP4) and non-structural regions P2 and P3 [13]. The 2B protein, together with 2A (protease) [14,15] and 2C (helicase/ATPase) [16–18], constitutes the P2 region of the viral genome. Whereas 2A and 3C perform well-defined enzymatic functions, namely the proteolytic cleavage of viral and host targets [19,20], 2B is remarkable for its broad functional repertoire. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.The 2B protein is a non-structural protein of approximately 100 amino acids, encoded by the enterovirus genome [21,22]. Since its discovery in the 1980s, it has been defined as a “viroporin,” a protein that disrupts ion homeostasis by forming transmembrane hydrophilic pores [23–25]. Across viral families, viroporins share conserved strategies of membrane perturbation, including pore formation, lipid bilayer disordering, and membrane curvature sensing, underscoring the evolutionary convergence of these mechanisms [26,27]. Well-characterized examples include HCV p7, influenza A M2, and Human Immunodeficiency Virus type 1 (HIV-1) Vpu, each of which exploits distinct membrane-targeting mechanisms while sharing a common capacity to dysregulate host ion homeostasis [28–31]. The enterovirus 2B protein extends this paradigm with a uniquely dynamic topology that may enable membrane stress sensing. This framework, which has dominated research for three decades, successfully explains the effects of 2B on calcium signaling and membrane permeability during early viral replication. However, intensive research over the past decade has revealed a functional breadth that far exceeds the scope of traditional pore models. A direct RNA-modification link between 2B and ferroptosis was established in a recent study [44].In summary, the existing framework can no longer accommodate the functional breadth and depth of 2B. These environmental parameters include lipid composition, membrane curvature, and pH values. Conformation-locking mutants exhibit directional changes in their functional spectra.Membrane microenvironment is essential for functional switchingThe functional switching of 2B strictly depends on changes in the membrane environmental parameters. (ii) Inferred from indirect evidence: conclusions consistent with the available data but not yet confirmed by direct experimentation. (iii) Speculative: components of the membrane stress sensor hypothesis that generate testable predictions but currently lack experimental support. full_text_sections.abstract: ABSTRACTEnterovirus 2B is a highly conserved, functionally versatile, nonstructural protein. The classic viroporin model, which restricts its role to ion channel formation, cannot account for its interactions with host factors such as Bcl-2-associated X protein, interleukin enhancer-binding factor 2, and karyopherin subunit alpha 1, nor its functional divergence among enteroviruses. We propose a novel, testable membrane stress sensor hypothesis: the transmembrane helices of 2B sense lipid composition and pH changes, and through conformational dynamics, spatiotemporally coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis, and immune evasion. We elaborate on this framework across six dimensions: structure–function mapping, calcium signaling, cell death pathways, immune evasion, evolutionary footprint, and antiviral targeting, along with cross-virus comparisons. We highlight key evidence gaps and limitations, and propose several future research directions. This framework establishes a mechanistic foundation for understanding 2B function and guiding rational anti-enteroviral drug designs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to address the functional pleiotropy of nonstructural protein 2B, which has hindered rational drug design for human enteroviruses. The traditional viroporin model, which limits 2B to ion channel formation, fails to explain its interactions with host factors and functional divergence among enteroviruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a theoretical and computational analysis of the enterovirus 2B protein, focusing on its role in human enteroviruses. It examines the protein's interactions with host factors and its functional divergence across different serotypes, including EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, and CV-A16.
analysis.methods: The study employs computational modeling and structural analysis to propose a framework in which the 2B protein functions as a membrane stress sensor. It explores conformational dynamics, lipid composition, pH changes, and their impact on calcium signaling, cell death pathways, and immune evasion.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that the transmembrane helices of 2B sense changes in the membrane microenvironment, including lipid composition, pH, and curvature. It also highlights the protein's direct interactions with host factors such as Bax, NLRP3, and KPNA1, and its role in coordinating calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, and immune evasion.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret their findings as supporting a novel hypothesis that the 2B protein acts as a membrane stress sensor, which provides a unified explanation for its diverse functions. This framework introduces a new perspective on 2B's role, moving beyond the traditional viroporin model.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The framework offers a mechanistic foundation for understanding 2B's role in enterovirus pathogenesis, which can guide the development of rational anti-enteroviral drugs. It also highlights key evidence gaps that need to be addressed for further research.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges key uncertainties, such as whether 2B exhibits calcium ion selectivity or forms a nonselective pore, and whether the pH dependence of EVD68 2B is mediated by a specific histidine residue. These limitations suggest that the evidence is moderate, requiring further experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study proposes a novel framework in which the enterovirus 2B protein functions as a membrane stress sensor, overcoming the limitations of the traditional viroporin model. The research highlights the protein's ability to sense changes in the membrane microenvironment, including lipid composition, pH, and curvature, and coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, and immune evasion. The findings suggest that 2B interacts with host factors such as Bax, NLRP3, and KPNA1, and its functional divergence among different enteroviruses may be explained by this new model. The study identifies key uncertainties, such as calcium ion selectivity and pH dependence, which require further experimental validation. The framework provides a mechanistic basis for understanding 2B's role in enterovirus pathogenesis and may inform future drug design efforts. However, the evidence is moderate due to the need for additional studies to confirm the proposed mechanisms.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to address the functional pleiotropy of nonstructural protein 2B, which has hindered rational drug design for human enteroviruses. The traditional viroporin model, which limits 2B to ion channel formation, fails to explain its interactions with host factors and functional divergence among enteroviruses.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a theoretical and computational analysis of the enterovirus 2B protein, focusing on its role in human enteroviruses. It examines the protein's interactions with host factors and its functional divergence across different serotypes, including EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, and CV-A16.
elements_en.methods: The study employs computational modeling and structural analysis to propose a framework in which the 2B protein functions as a membrane stress sensor. It explores conformational dynamics, lipid composition, pH changes, and their impact on calcium signaling, cell death pathways, and immune evasion.
elements_en.main_results: The study reports that the transmembrane helices of 2B sense changes in the membrane microenvironment, including lipid composition, pH, and curvature. It also highlights the protein's direct interactions with host factors such as Bax, NLRP3, and KPNA1, and its role in coordinating calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, and immune evasion.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret their findings as supporting a novel hypothesis that the 2B protein acts as a membrane stress sensor, which provides a unified explanation for its diverse functions. This framework introduces a new perspective on 2B's role, moving beyond the traditional viroporin model.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The framework offers a mechanistic foundation for understanding 2B's role in enterovirus pathogenesis, which can guide the development of rational anti-enteroviral drugs. It also highlights key evidence gaps that need to be addressed for further research.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges key uncertainties, such as whether 2B exhibits calcium ion selectivity or forms a nonselective pore, and whether the pH dependence of EVD68 2B is mediated by a specific histidine residue. These limitations suggest that the evidence is moderate, requiring further experimental validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决非结构蛋白 2B 的功能多效性,该多效性阻碍了 人肠道病毒 的合理药物设计。传统的病毒孔蛋白模型将 2B 限制为离子通道的形成,无法解释其与 宿主 因子的相互作用以及肠道病毒之间的功能差异。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对肠道病毒 2B 蛋白的理论和计算分析,重点关注其在 人肠道病毒 中的作用。它检查了该蛋白质与 宿主 因子的相互作用及其在不同血清型(包括 EV-A71、EV-D68、CV-A6 和 CV-A16)之间的功能差异。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用计算模型和结构分析提出了一个框架,其中 2B 蛋白充当膜应力传感器。它探讨了构象动力学、脂质组成、pH 变化及其对钙信号传导、细胞死亡途径和免疫逃避的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究报告称,2B 的跨膜螺旋可以感知膜微环境的变化,包括脂质成分、pH 值和曲率。它还强调了该蛋白与 Bax、NLRP3 和 KPNA1 等 宿主 因子的直接相互作用,及其在协调钙信号传导、细胞死亡途径选择和免疫逃避中的作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为支持一个新的假设,即 2B 蛋白充当膜应激传感器,这为其不同的功能提供了统一的解释。该框架超越了传统的病毒孔蛋白模型,引入了关于 2B 作用的新视角。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架为理解2B在肠道病毒发病机制中的作用提供了机制基础,可以指导合理的抗肠道病毒药物的开发。它还强调了进一步研究需要解决的关键证据差距。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认了一些关键的不确定性,例如 2B 是否表现出钙离子选择性或形成非选择性孔,以及 EVD68 2B 的 pH 依赖性是否由特定组氨酸残基介导。这些局限性表明证据是中等的,需要进一步的实验验证。

papers.source_body_en: Supplementary MaterialSupplementary data.docx Conclusions and outlookThis study proposes an integrative framework in which the enterovirus 2B protein acts as a “membrane stress sensor,” thereby overcoming the limitations of the traditional viroporin model. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.Enteroviruses possess a single-stranded, positive-sense RNA genome of approximately 7.5 kb in length [10–12]. Understanding how a single ~100-amino-acid protein can engage in such disparate pathways is the central question addressed in this review.The 2B protein is a non-structural protein of approximately 100 amino acids, encoded by the enterovirus genome [21,22]. A direct RNA-modification link between 2B and ferroptosis was established in a recent study [44].In summary, the existing framework can no longer accommodate the functional breadth and depth of 2B. Therefore, this study proposes a new theoretical framework: defining 2B as a membrane stress sensor, whose diverse functional outputs arise from its conformational responsiveness to changes in the membrane microenvironment. ABSTRACTEnterovirus 2B is a highly conserved, functionally versatile, nonstructural protein. The classic viroporin model, which restricts its role to ion channel formation, cannot account for its interactions with host factors such as Bcl-2-associated X protein, interleukin enhancer-binding factor 2, and karyopherin subunit alpha 1, nor its functional divergence among enteroviruses. papers.abstract_zh: 补充材料补充数据.docx 结论与展望本研究提出了一种整合框架,其中肠道病毒2B蛋白充当一种“膜应激传感器”,从而克服了传统病毒孔蛋白模型的局限性。理解一个约100个氨基酸的蛋白如何参与如此多样的通路是本文综述的核心问题。肠道病毒具有约7.5 kb长度的单链正链RNA基因组[10–12]。理解一个约100个氨基酸的蛋白如何参与如此多样的通路是本文综述的核心问题。2B蛋白是一种约100个氨基酸的非结构蛋白,由肠道病毒RNA编码[21,22]。最近的一项研究建立了2B与铁死亡之间的直接RNA修饰联系[44]。总之,现有的框架已无法容纳2B蛋白的功能广度和深度。因此,本研究提出一个新的理论框架:将2B定义为一种膜应激传感器,其多样化的功能输出源于其对膜微环境变化的构象响应。摘要肠道病毒2B是一种高度保守、功能多样的非结构蛋白。经典的病毒孔蛋白模型将其作用限制在离子通道形成,无法解释其与如Bcl-2相关X蛋白、白介素增强因子2和核转运亚基α1等因子的相互作用,以及其在肠道病毒中的功能分化。我们提出一个新颖且可检验的膜应激传感器假说:2B的跨膜螺旋能够感知脂质组成和pH变化,并通过构象动态,在时空上协调钙信号传导、细胞死亡等过程。

papers.title: Virological and epidemiological investigations of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak, Vietnam, 2023
papers.abstract: We report on the virological and epidemiological features of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak in Vietnam in 2023. Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) subgenogroup B5, first emerging around November 2022, and imported into Vietnam through a single introduction, was the primary cause. Convalescent plasma collected from patients infected with subgenogroups B5 in 2014 and 2023 could neutralize both contemporary viruses with comparable titers, suggesting no evidence of immune evasion. However, at one and six months before the start of the outbreak, only 6.7% of 0- < 3 year-old children in Ho Chi Minh City, an epicenter of the outbreak, had neutralizing antibodies against EV-A71. Seroprevalence increased as the outbreak progressed, coinciding with a drop in EV-A71 infected patients residing in Ho Chi Minh City, suggesting that serosurveillance could be a useful tool to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. Our collective findings have provided novel insights into the epidemiological factors driving EV-A71 emergence, and therefore would inform outbreak preparedness and response, and in particular the development of serosurveillance-based approach to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. EV-A71 infection represents an ongoing public health threat, currently affecting countries in the Asia-Pacific region, but with a high potential to become a global problem, and therefore should be closely monitored.

papers.title: Flavaglines as cross-kingdom translation inhibitors: Heavy halides at C6 potentiate antineoplastic, antiviral, and antifungal activities.
papers.abstract: The growing prevalence of cancer, coupled with the rise of multidrug-resistant pathogens, presents a formidable challenge to modern medicine. The flavagline class of secondary metabolites has been shown to possess a unique capacity to target multiple conserved pathways across various human malignancies and microbial pathogens. While numerous structure-activity relationship (SAR) campaigns have established trends with respect to specific indications, cross-kingdom comparative analyses have not been reported to date. In this work, a structurally diverse library comprising 17 novel and 5 natural flavagline analogues, alongside 3 known derivatives, was synthesized and systematically screened for cytotoxicity against five cancer cell lines, inhibition of Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), and activity against multidrug-resistant Candida and Aspergillus pathogens. It was found that introduction of heavy halides (Br or I) at the 6 position significantly potentiates the in vitro biological activities of all tested flavagline chemotypes. Immunoblotting experiments, circumstantial evidence, and molecular docking suggest that the enhanced activity of C6-Br derivatives is consistent with enhanced DEAD-box helicase (eIF4A or DDX3)-RNA clamping. Additionally, the putative flavagline biogenetic precursor chemotypes, aglains and flavonols, were shown to exhibit significant antiviral and antifungal activities. This is the first systematic SAR study directly comparing the anticancer and antipathogenic activities of flavagline derivatives, or any other known translation inhibitors.

papers.title_zh: 黄黄素作为跨界翻译抑制剂:C6 处的重卤化物可增强抗肿瘤、抗病毒药物 和抗真菌活性。
papers.source_body_en: The growing prevalence of cancer, coupled with the rise of multidrug-resistant pathogens, presents a formidable challenge to modern medicine. The flavagline class of secondary metabolites has been shown to possess a unique capacity to target multiple conserved pathways across various human malignancies and microbial pathogens. While numerous structure-activity relationship (SAR) campaigns have established trends with respect to specific indications, cross-kingdom comparative analyses have not been reported to date. In this work, a structurally diverse library comprising 17 novel and 5 natural flavagline analogues, alongside 3 known derivatives, was synthesized and systematically screened for cytotoxicity against five cancer cell lines, inhibition of Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), and activity against multidrug-resistant Candida and Aspergillus pathogens. It was found that introduction of heavy halides (Br or I) at the 6 position significantly potentiates the in vitro biological activities of all tested flavagline chemotypes. Immunoblotting experiments, circumstantial evidence, and molecular docking suggest that the enhanced activity of C6-Br derivatives is consistent with enhanced DEAD-box helicase (eIF4A or DDX3)-RNA clamping. Additionally, the putative flavagline biogenetic precursor chemotypes, aglains and flavonols, were shown to exhibit significant antiviral and antifungal activities. This is the first systematic SAR study directly comparing the anticancer and antipathogenic activities of flavagline derivatives, or any other known translation inhibitors.
papers.abstract_zh: 癌症的不断增长,加上多重耐药病原体的兴起,对现代医学提出了巨大的挑战。黄黄素类次生代谢物已被证明具有独特的能力,可以靶向多种人类恶性肿瘤和微生物病原体的多个保守途径。虽然许多结构-活动关系(SAR)活动已经确定了特定适应症的趋势,但迄今为止尚未报告跨领域的比较分析。在这项工作中,合成了一个结构多样化的文库,包含 17 种新型和 5 种天然黄黄碱类似物以及 3 种已知衍生物,并系统地筛选了其对 5 种癌细胞系的细胞毒性、对肠道病毒 A71 (EV-A71) 的抑制作用以及对多重耐药念珠菌和曲霉病原体的活性。结果发现,在 6 位引入重卤化物(Br 或 I)可显着增强所有测试的黄黄碱化学型的体外生物活性。免疫印迹实验、间接证据和分子对接表明,C6-Br 衍生物的增强活性与增强的 DEAD-box 解旋酶(eIF4A 或 DDX3)-RNA 钳制一致。此外,假定的黄黄素生物遗传前体化学型、黄酮素和黄酮醇,显示出显着的 抗病毒药物 和抗真菌活性。这是第一个系统的 SAR 研究,直接比较黄黄素衍生物或任何其他已知翻译抑制剂的抗癌和抗病原体活性。

papers.title: Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study
papers.abstract: Background In China, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) persists as a prevalent infectious disease with high transmissibility. Nevertheless, the link between environmental determinants and HFMD incidence has not been fully elucidated. The study assessed associations between air pollution, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence in Shenzhen, China, while also evaluating shifts in these associations before and after the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and during the COVID-19 epidemic. Methods Daily data on HFMD cases, air pollutants (such as PM 2.5 , PM 10 , SO 2 , NO 2 , CO, and O 3 ), and meteorological variables (including mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed) were collected for the period from 2013 to 2022. Associations were assessed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), accounting for immediate and delayed effects. Results Spearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO2 showing delayed effects. However, SO2 unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. NO2 exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O3 showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM 2.5 and PM 10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature exhibited a dual-peak risk pattern at extremely low and extremely high temperatures, with extreme heat producing sustained effects and extreme cold shorter-lived risk. HFMD risk increased under conditions of extremely high humidity. In general, the risk associated with atmospheric pressure rose as pressure levels increased, and asymmetric lagged effects were observed at both low- and high-concentration extremes. Extremely high wind speed causing short-term harm and extremely low wind speed leading to delayed cumulative risk. Conclusion Meteorological factors exhibit more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查中国深圳环境空气污染和气象因素与手足口病 (HFMD) 风险之间的关联,重点是了解这些关系如何因肠道病毒 71 疫苗 和 COVID-19 流行等公共卫生干预措施而随着时间的推移而发生变化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项时间序列研究分析了中国深圳 2013 年至 2022 年手足口病病例和环境因素的每日数据,涵盖广泛的污染物和气象变量。该研究将空气污染和气象数据作为分析的关键组成部分。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用分布式滞后非线性模型(DLNM)来评估空气污染物、气象条件和手足口病 发病率 之间的关联,同时考虑了即时影响和延迟影响。Spearman相关分析也用于评估手足口病与各种环境因素之间的关系。
elements_zh.main_results: Spearman相关分析显示,手足口病与SO2、平均气温、相对湿度、风速呈正相关,与PM2.5、PM10、NO2、CO、大气压力呈负相关。DLNM 模型显示,SO2 和 CO 在极高浓度下都会增加累积风险,其中 SO2 显示出延迟效应。尽管整体呈下降趋势,但二氧化氮在极端浓度下仍表现出 U 形风险。O3 表现出双峰,滞后 1 后在极高浓度下具有保护作用。PM2.5 和 PM10 在低浓度下表现出风险峰,但在极高浓度下具有保护作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,与空气污染物相比,气象因素与手足口病的关联性更强,这凸显了需要进一步研究环境变量与疾病之间复杂的相互作用。该研究的新颖之处在于它随着时间的推移对这些关联进行了全面评估,纳入了公共卫生干预措施造成的变化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持对可能影响手足口病风险的气象因素进行有针对性的公共卫生干预,可能为深圳和类似城市环境的疾病 监测 和预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据因其对观察数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入混杂因素。由于环境与疾病相互作用的复杂性以及未测量的变量可能影响结果,因此研究结果的可信度为中等。

papers.title: Discovery of antivirals against enteroviruses by targeting viral non-structural protein 2C and structural protein VP1
papers.abstract: Enteroviruses (EVs), including EV-D68, EV-A71, and coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3), impose a substantial global disease burden, yet no antiviral therapies are currently approved. In this thesis, we developed two antiviral strategies targeting the highly conserved nonstructural protein 2C and the viral capsid protein VP1. In the first part of the thesis, structure-property relationship (SPR) studies led to the identification of the promising 2C inhibitor Jun6504, which exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple enterovirus strains and favorable pharmacokinetic properties. In a neonatal mouse model of EV-D68-induced paralysis, Jun6504 demonstrated significant antiviral efficacy. To address the lack of direct biochemical assays for enteroviral 2C inhibitors, we developed a fluorescence polarization (FP)-based binding assay targeting a conserved allosteric pocket in enteroviral 2C proteins, enabling direct and quantitative measurement of inhibitor binding affinity and facilitating target-based inhibitor discovery and optimization. In parallel, structure-based optimization of a virtual screening hit yielded the VP1-targeting inhibitors Jun11695 and Jun11787, which exhibited nanomolar antiviral potency against EV-D68 and micromolar activity against EV-A71 and CVB3. Both inhibitors demonstrated complementary evidence of VP1 target engagement, favorable pharmacokinetic properties, and significant reductions in viral loads and paralysis progression in vivo. To overcome the low genetic barrier to resistance associated with conventional VP1 capsid inhibitors, we further developed Jun15702, a first-in-class VP1-targeting degrader. Jun15702 exhibited potent antiviral activity against multiple wild-type EV-D68 strains and retained submicromolar potency against the recombinant pleconaril-resistant variant rMO-VP1 F159V. Mechanistic studies demonstrated the distinct dual mode-of-action of Jun15702 that not only inhibited viral entry but also induced CRBN-dependent degradation of VP1 when administered after viral entry. Collectively, these studies establish enteroviral 2C and VP1 as therapeutically tractable antiviral targets and provide complementary occupancy-driven and targeted protein degradation strategies for developing next-generation antivirals against enterovirus infections.

elements_zh.methods: 结构-性质关系 (SPR) 研究鉴定出了有前景的 2C 抑制剂 Jun6504,并对虚拟筛选结果进行基于结构的优化,产生了 VP1 靶向抑制剂 Jun11695 和 Jun11787。

papers.abstract_zh: 肠道病毒 (EV),包括 EV-D68、EV-A71 和柯萨奇病毒 B3 (CVB3),给全球带来了巨大的疾病负担,但目前尚无 抗病毒药物 疗法获得批准。在本论文中,我们针对高度保守的非结构蛋白2C和病毒衣壳蛋白VP1开发了两种抗病毒药物策略。在论文的第一部分,结构-性质关系(SPR)研究鉴定出了有前景的2C抑制剂Jun6504,它对多种肠道病毒株表现出广谱抗病毒药物活性和良好的药代动力学特性。在 EV-D68 诱导的瘫痪新生小鼠模型中,Jun6504 表现出显着的 抗病毒药物 功效。为了解决肠道病毒 2C 抑制剂缺乏直接生化检测的问题,我们开发了一种基于荧光偏振 (FP) 的结合检测,针对肠道病毒 2C 蛋白中的保守变构袋,从而能够直接定量测量抑制剂结合亲和力,并促进基于目标的抑制剂发现和优化。与此同时,基于结构的虚拟筛选结果优化产生了 VP1 靶向抑制剂 Jun11695 和 Jun11787,它们对 EV-D68 表现出纳摩尔 抗病毒药物 效力,对 EV-A71 和 CVB3 表现出微摩尔活性。两种抑制剂都证明了 VP1 靶点参与、有利的药代动力学特性以及体内病毒载量和麻痹进展显着减少的互补证据。为了克服与传统 VP1 衣壳抑制剂相关的低遗传耐药性障碍,我们进一步开发了 Jun15702,这是一种一流的 VP1 靶向降解剂。Jun15702 对多种野生型 EV-D68 菌株表现出有效的 抗病毒药物 活性,并保留了对重组普来可那利抗性变体 rMO-VP1 F159V 的亚微摩尔效力。机制研究表明,Jun15702 具有独特的双重作用模式,在病毒进入后给药时,不仅能抑制病毒进入,还能诱导 VP1 依赖于 CRBN 的降解。总的来说,这些研究将肠道病毒 2C 和 VP1 确定为治疗上易于处理的 抗病毒药物 靶点,并为开发下一代抗肠道病毒感染的 抗病毒药物 提供补充的占用驱动和靶向蛋白质降解策略。

papers.full_text: AbstractEmerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. As an unbiased and noninvasive population-level surveillance approach, wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as an urban-scale monitoring tool for proactively capturing the community disease burden. In this study, metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were employed to preliminarily characterize wastewater viral communities in Gansu Province from 2024 to 2026. Across the three annual sampling groups, the Simpson diversity index calculated from metagenomic taxonomic profiles showed a significant negative correlation with sampling year. Despite viral enrichment, more than 97% of sequencing reads were assigned to bacteria, likely reflecting residual nonviral nucleic acids and limitations in metagenomic classification. The wastewater virome exhibited a complex host-association spectrum, within which bacteriophages and plant-associated viruses displayed relatively stable community structures and high relative abundances. Among human pathogens, astroviruses were consistently detected at high relative abundances across all samples. Human astrovirus 1 accounted for the largest proportion, and a nearly complete genome sequence of the extraintestinal infection-associated astrovirus MLB2 was recovered. Targeted sequencing further revealed a highly structured environmental enterovirus profile dominated by the species Enterovirus betacoxsackie, followed by Enterovirus alphacoxsackie, whereas Enterovirus coxsackiepol was detected at an extremely low abundance and Enterovirus deconjuncti was not detected. In addition to several common viruses associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease, rare viruses, including coxsackievirus A19 and enterovirus B83, were successfully captured. Echovirus 11 was identified as the predominant enterovirus serotype in current wastewater surveillance in Gansu Province. In summary, this study provides a preliminary characterization of the viral community profiles in wastewater samples from Gansu Province, demonstrates the effectiveness of wastewater-based epidemiology for population-level surveillance, and underscores the need to establish a coordinated defense network integrating clinical case surveillance with environmental monitoring.Keywords: astroviruses, enterovirus, Gansu Province, metagenomic sequencing, targeted next-generation sequencing, wastewater Materials and methodsCollection and processing of the wastewater samplesBetween 2024 and 2026, 18 raw wastewater samples were collected from wastewater treatment plants across 6 cities in Gansu Province (Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Dingxi). Based on their respective sampling years, the samples were categorized into 3 groups: GS24, GS25, and GS26. Seasonal patterns, population differences, and other demographic factors were not considered when defining these groups. Specifically, the sample groups were designated as follows: GS24-1 to GS24-6 were collected in July 2024 from Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Hezuo, respectively; GS25-1 to GS25-6 were collected in June 2025 from Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Zhangye, respectively; and GS26-1 to GS26-6 were collected in March 2026 from Hezuo, Zhangye, Lanzhou, Jiuquan, Longnan, and Dingxi, respectively. GS24-1 and GS24-6 were independently collected on the same day from the same wastewater treatment plant in Hezuo. The same applied to GS25-2 and GS25-6 in Zhangye. The collection dates reflected operational availability and were not selected to provide seasonally matched observations. At each monitoring site, 1 L of raw wastewater was collected. The samples were transported at 4 °C to the laboratory of Gansu Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention within 7 days and processed immediately upon arrival (Wang et al., 2014). For viral concentration, the wastewater samples were initially centrifuged at 1,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Subsequently, 2.5 M MgCl2 was added to the supernatant to achieve a final concentration of 0.05 M, and the pH was adjusted to 3.5 using 0.5 N HCl. The prepared solution was then filtered through a 142-mm cellulose nitrate membrane using a positive-pressure pump. Following filtration, the membrane was fragmented and eluted twice with 10 mL of 3% beef extract by vortexing on ice for 5 min each time. The pooled eluates were centrifuged at 1,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C and finally passed through a 0.22 μm syringe filter.Nucleic acid extraction and sequencingTotal nucleic acid extraction was performed using the High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid Kit (Roche) without DNase digestion. To reduce potential false-positive results associated with the increased PCR cycles required for capture-based sequencing, the initial extract was divided for parallel and independent library preparations. Metagenomic libraries were generated with the MGIEasy Fast RNA Library Prep Set, whereas the IGT® Fast Stranded RNA Library Prep Kit v2.0 was applied for capture-based construction. For targeted enrichment, a custom enterovirus probe panel was deployed; this panel was specifically designed for selected viruses, encompassing the species Enterovirus alphacoxsackie, Enterovirus betacoxsackie, Enterovirus coxsackiepol, and Enterovirus deconjuncti. Negative controls were processed in parallel during nucleic acid extraction and library preparation to monitor potential contamination, and no evidence of contamination or other procedural abnormalities was observed. Finally, paired-end reads were generated by sequencing the prepared libraries on a DNBSEQ-T7 platform.Sequence data analysisRaw sequencing reads generated by the metagenomic and targeted-capture workflows were assessed using FastQC1 before downstream analysis. No sequencing dataset was excluded from downstream analysis solely on the basis of the FastQC assessment. For raw paired-end reads, adapter trimming and quality filtering (length <50 bp, quality score <20, or containing N bases) were performed using KneadData.2 High-quality reads were then aligned to the human reference genome (hg19) via Bowtie2 to discard host sequences, with the unmapped reads kept for subsequent analyses (Langmead and Salzberg, 2012). Metagenomic reads were taxonomically classified using Kraken2 across multiple taxonomic levels (Wood et al., 2019). All sequencing reads were assembled using MEGAHIT (Li et al., 2015). Contigs (length ≥300 bp, coverage ≥3×) were filtered via awk and annotated using blastn, taking the highest bitscore as the final assignment (Chen et al., 2015). Read abundances per viral species were quantified using BWA-backtrack for downstream evaluation (Li and Durbin, 2009). All astrovirus- and enterovirus-associated contigs assembled using MEGAHIT were extracted from each sample and individually re-evaluated using NCBI BLASTn.3Rarefaction analysis and diversity visualizationAll statistical analyses and data visualizations were performed using R 4.4.3 software.4 Specifically, alpha diversity was assessed at the genus level, and the Shannon and inverse Simpson indices were calculated using the vegan package. Hereafter, the term “Simpson index” refers specifically to the inverse Simpson formulation (1/D). Temporal trends in alpha diversity were assessed using one-tailed Spearman’s rank correlation tests, with the a priori hypothesis that diversity indices would decline over sampling years. Spearman’s rho (ρ) values and corresponding one-sided p values were calculated to evaluate the monotonic relationship between sampling year and alpha diversity indices. Rarefaction curves, heatmaps, stacked bar plots, and visualizations of alpha diversity indices were generated using the ggplot2 package.Quantitative profiling of the viromeFor the quantitative analysis of viral communities, relative abundances were estimated using the reads per million normalization method described in Equation 1. The mapped read counts of each viral contig were adjusted for genome length differences by dividing the read counts by the average genome size of the corresponding viral family or genus. Subsequently, the adjusted read counts were normalized against the total number of reads assigned to all viral families or genera within each individual sample (Worp et al., 2025). This normalization strategy was consistently applied to all heatmaps generated in this study.However, a modified approach was applied for the stacked bar charts illustrating the relative abundances of different species within the genus Enterovirus. Because genome lengths among enterovirus serotypes are highly conserved, with an average size of approximately 7.4 kb, genome length normalization was omitted when calculating the relative abundance of enterovirus-associated contigs.(1)Relative abundance=virus readsaverage genome length×total viral reads×106The host type classifications for the viral families listed herein were retrieved from the Virus-Host Database.5Comparison of viral diversityTo compare viral community structure across sample groups, principal component analysis (PCA) was performed on centered log-ratio transformed abundance data (Gloor et al., 2017). Zero counts in the abundance matrices were replaced with a pseudocount equivalent to half of the minimum positive abundance value detected within the respective dataset, as centered log-ratio transformation requires strictly positive values. Viral taxa contributing most strongly to the principal components were identified based on the magnitude of their loadings. PCA biplots were generated using the ggplot2 package in R 4.4.3 software, with 68% confidence ellipses overlaid to visualize group clustering.Phylogenetic analysisReference viral VP1 gene sequences were retrieved from GenBank at the National Center for biotechnology information (NCBI). These sequences, together with the VP1 sequences generated in this study, were aligned using MAFFT v7.520 (Katoh and Standley, 2013). Neighbor-joining (NJ) phylogenetic trees were constructed in MEGA7 based on evolutionary distances calculated using the maximum composite likelihood method (Kumar et al., 2016). The robustness of the inferred tree topologies was assessed by bootstrap analysis with 1,000 replicates (Felsenstein, 1985), and bootstrap support values of 70% or higher were displayed at the corresponding nodes. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2026.1966428/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials ResultsBetween-year variation in alpha diversity and broad taxonomic compositionRarefaction analysis showed that the sequencing captured most of the detectable genus-level diversity across the three sampling groups, indicating that the sequencing depth was sufficient (Figure 1A). Overall metagenomic sequencing statistics and alpha diversity indices (including the Shannon and Simpson indices) are summarized in Table 1 and visualized in Figures 1B,C. Sampling year was treated as an ordinal variable. The Shannon index showed a negative but nonsignificant correlation with sampling year (Spearman’s ρ = −0.354, p = 0.075). In contrast, the Simpson index exhibited a significant negative correlation with sampling year (Spearman’s ρ = −0.472, p = 0.024). Given that the dataset comprised only three annual sampling campaigns conducted in different months, these analyses were considered exploratory assessments of between-year variation. At the broadest taxonomic level, more than 97% of reads in each dataset were assigned to Bacteria, whereas no more than 0.94% were classified as viral (Table 2). Following taxonomic classification with Kraken2, 56.42–74.74% of the metagenomic reads across samples remained unclassified at the genus level (Supplementary Table S1). In this context, “unclassified” indicates that the reference database and parameter settings did not provide sufficient evidence for a reliable taxonomic assignment. The unclassified reads were not subjected to further characterization in this study.Figure 1Overview of metagenomic sequencing data across the three groups. (A) Rarefaction curves at the genus level.
